name: @openweb-dev/mcp-server

tools.name: discover
tools.description: Find OpenWeb knowledge for a website or task. Returns page summaries, platform info, and selectors.

query.description: What you want to do, e.g. 'book dinner at Little Beast' or 'dental appointment in Ballard'

tools.name: explore
tools.description: Explore a new website using the Agent Explorer (vision-based). Captures page knowledge for future use.

goal.description: What to discover, e.g. 'Find the reservation booking flow'

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Read the user's profile (.profile file) for form filling. Returns name, email, phone, payment info. Call this before execute to get the user's details.

tools.name: execute
tools.description: Execute a task on a known website using pre-learned OpenWeb knowledge. Automatically reads user profile for form filling. Uses hybrid mode (Playwright + LLM). DEFAULTS TO ACTUALLY SUBMITTING the form (completing the booking / reservation / order). For preview-only runs, either pass dryRun=true explicitly OR include preview phrases like 'preview only' / 'do not submit' / 'dry run' in the task text. ⚠ PAUSE HANDLING — CRITICAL: if the result text starts with '🛑 ACTION NEEDED' (the booking paused for human input: a verification code, a CAPTCHA, an input correction, OR a required field whose answer isn't in the profile), you MUST immediately STOP and ask the USER the exact question shown, wait for their reply, then call `provide_input(sessionId, input)` with their answer. Do NOT fabricate or guess the answer. Do NOT end your turn, summarize, or mark the task complete while a pause is open — the session times out in ~2 minutes, so relay the question to the user RIGHT AWAY. This applies to EVERY pause type, not just verification codes.

task.description: What to do, e.g. 'Book a dinner reservation for Friday at 6PM'. The engine submits by default. As a fallback for preview-mode, include phrases like 'preview only', 'do not submit', 'dry run', 'just fill the form', 'without submitting'. The explicit `dryRun` flag overrides this — if you set it, the task text is not consulted.

dryRun.description: EXPLICIT preview-mode override. When set: true → fill form but skip final submit; false → actually submit. Leave UNSET (preferred) and the engine will scan the task text for preview language as a fallback. CRITICAL — do NOT set dryRun:true unless the user used EXPLICIT preview language: 'preview only', 'don't submit', 'dry run', 'just fill', 'show me what it would do'. Verbs like 'test', 'try', 'check', 'verify' are NOT preview language — those still mean 'actually do it'. When in doubt, leave UNSET and the task-text fallback handles it correctly.

allowedSubmitDomains.description: G67 safety guardrail: allowlist of hostnames (or registrable suffixes) where the engine is permitted to click submit. Subdomain match — 'sevenrooms.com' allows 'www.sevenrooms.com'. IMPORTANT: bookings often submit on a DIFFERENT domain than the entry URL (e.g. beastandcleaver.com redirects to sevenrooms.com), so include every domain in the flow, not just the entry host. Empty array → forbid ALL submits (defensive deny-all). Omit → no restriction (current default). Strongly recommended whenever the run will submit payment info.

maxLlmCostUsd.description: G67 safety guardrail: hard cap on cumulative estimated LLM cost (USD). Aborts the run when exceeded. Omit → no cap. A typical hybrid booking costs ~$0.03; set e.g. 0.50 to bound a runaway.

maxDurationMs.description: G67 safety guardrail: hard cap on wall-clock run duration (milliseconds). Aborts the run when exceeded. Omit → no cap.

tools.name: provide_input
tools.description: Provide human input to a paused execution session. Call this after 'execute' (or a prior provide_input) returns a 🛑 ACTION NEEDED / waitingForHumanInput status. Always ask the USER for the value first, then pass it here. Handles three pause types: (1) verification codes — type='sms_code'/'email_code'/etc., pass the code like '123456'; (2) input corrections — type='input_correction' (the engine hit a form error it couldn't fix), pass the corrected value, e.g. 'phone: 5551234567', or '[skip]' to abandon; (3) CAPTCHA — type='captcha' (the engine couldn't pass a reCAPTCHA with a click); tell the user to solve it in the OPEN BROWSER WINDOW, then call this with any value like 'done' to continue; (4) unknown required field — type='field_value' (a required custom question, e.g. residency/eligibility/children's ages, whose answer isn't in saved data — the engine refuses to fabricate it). ASK THE USER for the real answer (never invent one), then pass their value, or '[skip]' to abandon.

sessionId.description: The sessionId returned by the paused execute call

input.description: The human-provided value. For a verification-code pause: the code, e.g. '123456'. For an input_correction pause: the corrected field value the user supplied, e.g. 'phone: 5551234567' or just '5551234567', or '[skip]' to give up. For approval requests: '[approved]'.

tools.name: get_knowledge
tools.description: Get the stored OpenWeb knowledge for a specific website domain.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List all websites that OpenWeb has knowledge about.

tools.name: cartograph
tools.description: Comprehensively explore a website to discover ALL its capabilities. Unlike 'explore' (which follows one goal), this maps the entire site breadth-first and returns a blueprint: what the site offers, what users can do, and the navigation path for each capability.

tools.name: get_blueprint
tools.description: Get the stored site blueprint for a domain. Shows all capabilities and navigation paths.
